name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Combat Exoskeleton Lite CEL-3
product_name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Combat Exoskeleton Lite CEL-3
description: A lightweight partial exoskeleton that augments the wearer's lower body and core strength without the bulk of a full tactical exoskeleton. The CEL-3 consists of articulated leg braces, a hip frame, and a spinal support strut that multiply lower body strength by a factor of 3 and increase sprint speed by 60%. The system is powered by a waist-mounted battery and controlled by neural interface or manual input, allowing the wearer to run at 45 km/h, jump 3 meters vertically, and carry loads up to 200 kg without fatigue. The CEL-3 fits under loose clothing, making it the preferred mobility enhancement for operators who need augmented physicality without visible hardware.
story_hooks: Security footage shows a suspect running at 45 km/h through a commercial district — far beyond human capability, but no visible augmentation. The CEL-3's concealed profile means witnesses describe an impossibly fast human.
A CEL-3 wearer experienced a servo lockup mid-stride at full speed — the resulting fall at 45 km/h was not survivable, and the manufacturer's logs show the lockup was triggered by an external signal.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek partial exoskeleton resembling articulated athletic support gear rather than heavy combat armor. The design prioritizes concealment with angular carbon-composite braces that hug the legs and spine, connected by a minimalist hip frame. The overall silhouette is deliberately low-profile—more compression suit than mechanical rig.
physical_description.dimensions: Leg braces extend from ankle to mid-thigh (~60 cm); spinal strut runs from sacrum to mid-back (~40 cm); hip frame spans ~25 cm across the pelvis. Total footprint when worn is human-scale, intentionally compact.
physical_description.weight_description: 4.5 kg total—handheld if disassembled, but worn as a distributed load across the body. Balanced enough that the wearer barely registers it after calibration.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-fiber composite chassis with reinforced titanium alloy at articulation joints. Synthetic muscle-weave actuators in matte charcoal gray.
physical_description.finish: Matte non-reflective composite with subtle brushed titanium accents at hinges. Designed to avoid chrome or glossy surfaces that would catch light during covert movement.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with darker charcoal carbon-weave panels. Accent struts in brushed steel. Minimalist aesthetic—no unnecessary visual noise.
physical_description.interface_elements: Waist-mounted battery unit (fist-sized, recessed into a hip pocket) with a small tactile interface panel. Optional neural-link port at the base of the spinal strut (recessed, barely visible). Manual override buttons disguised as equipment snaps along the leg braces. Barely-perceptible LED status indicators (blue idle, amber active, red overload) integrated into the hip frame.
distinctive_features: Articulated knee joints with visible mechanical linkages—clean, minimal design
Spinal strut that follows the body's natural curve rather than rigid framing
Hip frame constructed as a single carbon-weave piece that wraps around the pelvis
Battery unit shaped like a sleek modular component, designed to clip/unclip quickly
Ankle braces with subtle grip pads on the soles—visible only from underneath
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Small Murmuration Systems logo (stylized murmuration of birds forming a circuit symbol) embossed on the hip frame. Model designation 'CEL-3' stamped on battery unit. Faint regulatory stamps (GLMZ compliance, Tier 3+ certification) on the inner spinal strut.
physical_description.condition_typical: In use, barely visible under cargo pants or loose athletic wear. At rest on a workbench, the exoskeleton appears almost sculptural—a high-tech orthotic rather than armor. Slight shimmer from carbon-weave under workshop lighting. Battery unit glows faintly with ambient power indicator.
